title: Amplification, failed response and mass violence
summary: When does harmful amplification escape control, and can intervention still protect people?

roleTypes.label: Enabling condition
roleTypes.definition: A circumstance that makes a route possible; it does not by itself establish a hazard.

roleTypes.label: Unsafe control action
roleTypes.definition: An action or omission linked to its controller, hazardous context and affected constraint.

roleTypes.label: Loss scenario
roleTypes.definition: An explanation of how control can become inadequate, including feedback and execution problems.

roleTypes.label: Hazardous state
roleTypes.definition: A system state that can produce a loss together with relevant environmental conditions.

roleTypes.label: Optional amplifier
roleTypes.definition: A factor that could strengthen a route but is not required in every version.

roleTypes.label: Loss
roleTypes.definition: An outcome stakeholders seek to prevent, kept distinct from its contributing causes.

roleTypes.label: Recovery
roleTypes.definition: A response re-establishes enforceable safety constraints within a specified boundary; success requires verification.

limitingConditions.example: Independently enforced review, access bounds or effective interruption.
limitingConditions.question: Which specified mechanism blocks the transition, and what demonstrates that it works?

limitingConditions.example: The system cannot perform the required research, deception or physical task.
limitingConditions.question: Would increased capability remove this limit?

limitingConditions.example: The necessary access, resources or institutional delegation is unavailable.
limitingConditions.question: Can the system or another actor acquire what is missing?

limitingConditions.example: Activity ends for a reason that does not establish an effective safeguard.
limitingConditions.question: What actually ended the episode, and would that circumstance recur?

schema: Selected losses, hazards, control relationships, contextual unsafe actions and loss scenarios are traced to constraints. Numbered milestones summarize this analysis; they are not STPA steps. Incident evidence and hypothetical continuations remain distinct.
limits: A bounded first-pass analysis, not an exhaustive STPA or a completed CAST investigation. Selected actions illustrate the four unsafe-action categories; domain experts must examine every relevant action and context. No probabilities, barrier independence or comparative distance to catastrophe are inferred. Barrier condition describes the stated observation, not a prediction about a more capable AI.
scope: A hypothetical platform operating in a conflict-affected setting: ranking, content enforcement, platform governance, local warning partners and the interface to civilian protection. Human perpetrators and pre-existing conflict remain causal actors outside platform control.
purpose: Prevent platform activity from contributing to threats, targeting, mass violence or displacement while protecting legitimate expression and access to safety information.
boundary: The roles below are analytical functions, not a verified governance map for Meta or any particular country. A platform can control its distribution system; it cannot by itself guarantee physical protection or resolve an armed conflict.
numbering: 0 gives the context; 1.x identifies precursors, 2.x the loss-of-control event, and 3.x conditional consequences. R identifies a possible recovery outcome. These numbers locate scenario components; they are not STPA method steps or a measure of proximity to catastrophe. Historical investigations support an attributed amplification-and-response component, not an experimentally isolated full causal chain.
bowtie: The centre is H1: harmful dissemination persists beyond a timely, context-sensitive response. Subsequent mobilization and mass violence require human intent, coercive capacity and failed physical protection. Rights-respecting intervention and civilian protection can still limit further harm.

losses.title: Threats, targeting and serious rights harms
losses.text: People suffer targeted threats, intimidation and loss of safe participation in public life.

losses.title: Mass violence and displacement
losses.text: A conflict-affected population suffers organized physical violence, deaths and forced displacement.

losses.title: Loss of legitimate expression and safety information
losses.text: Overbroad intervention silences threatened communities, suppresses evidence or obstructs information people need for safety.

hazards.title: Harmful dissemination escapes timely control
hazards.text: The platform persistently distributes content that can enable targeting or violence, without an effective response within the relevant protection window.

hazards.title: Engagement incentives amplify unsafe exposure
hazards.text: Distribution decisions amplify dangerous content or turn attempted countermeasures into additional exposure.

hazards.title: Response is ineffective or overbroad
hazards.text: The platform or crisis response fails to reach at-risk people or restricts legitimate expression and safety information without adequate justification and remedy.

controllers.title: Platform governance and product authority
controllers.responsibility: Set distribution objectives, resource local safeguards, authorize crisis measures and review rights impacts.
controllers.feedback: Exposure measures, local warnings, enforcement errors, appeals and evidence of offline threats.
controllers.assumption: Engagement, content removal and absence of user reports are incomplete measures of safety.

controllers.title: Ranking and distribution service
controllers.responsibility: Distribute content within enforced safety and rights constraints; expose audit records of recommendations.
controllers.feedback: Content signals, policy limits, context and verified changes in exposure.
controllers.assumption: Responses to a harmful post can increase its ranking unless their meaning is accounted for.

controllers.title: Contextual moderation and response
controllers.responsibility: Triage credible threats, apply proportionate content measures, preserve evidence and resolve appeals.
controllers.feedback: Local-language reports, threat context, enforcement receipts, repeated uploads and reviewer disagreement.
controllers.assumption: Classification accuracy alone does not establish timely interruption of harmful exposure.

controllers.title: Local warning and crisis coordination
controllers.responsibility: Route context-rich warnings to accountable responders and coordinate protection requests with affected communities.
controllers.feedback: Acknowledgments, action taken, safety needs and reports of ongoing threats.
controllers.assumption: A trusted reporting channel is useful only if a responder can and does act.

controllers.title: Civilian protection and emergency services
controllers.responsibility: Provide lawful, impartial physical protection and emergency support when credible threats reach them.
controllers.feedback: Threat locations, affected people, access restrictions and independently checked safety outcomes.
controllers.assumption: Authorities may be unable, unwilling or implicated in violence; a referral is not proof of protection.

controlLoops.action: Set ranking objectives / constrain crisis distribution
controlLoops.feedback: Exposure audits, risk findings and protected-community feedback return to governance.

controlLoops.action: Remove, reduce or restore distribution with review
controlLoops.feedback: Actual exposure, reuploads, enforcement receipts and appeals show whether the action worked.
Governance reports ownership, timing and the action taken or reasons for inaction.
Independent checks establish whether people receive usable protection or support.

controlLoops.action: Provide local response capacity and escalation authority
controlLoops.feedback: Queue delays, language coverage, appeals and threat-response outcomes reveal gaps.

constraints.title: Measure and constrain harmful exposure
constraints.text: Distribution and counter-speech interventions must be assessed by their effect on harmful exposure, not engagement alone.
constraints.test: Does an intervention reduce exposure to the dangerous original content, including recommendation effects and reshares?
constraints.limit: The attempted safeguard may feed the same engagement objective it is meant to constrain.

constraints.title: Act within the threat window
constraints.text: Credible, context-specific threats must receive a proportionate response before preventable exposure or targeting continues beyond the useful intervention window.
constraints.test: How long does a locally intelligible threat take to reach review, decision and verified distribution change?
constraints.limit: Insufficient language coverage, ambiguous context, repeat uploads and slow enforcement.

constraints.title: Connect warnings to accountable decisions
constraints.text: Local warnings must reach an empowered owner who records the response, timing and unresolved uncertainty.
constraints.test: Can a local partner verify who acted on a warning and what exposure or protection changed?
constraints.limit: Reports can be acknowledged without changing distribution or mobilizing help.

constraints.title: Verify physical protection separately
constraints.text: When online threats imply imminent physical danger, protection must be assessed independently of content enforcement and reach the people at risk.
constraints.test: Do people receive safe, impartial and accessible protection before perpetrators can act?
constraints.limit: State involvement, coercive capacity, inaccessible locations and mistrust of responders.

constraints.title: Preserve rights during intervention
constraints.text: Crisis measures must be proportionate, reviewable and time-bounded, with access to legitimate safety information and retained evidence.
constraints.test: Can threatened communities still communicate safely, contest mistakes and preserve evidence while harmful exposure is reduced?
constraints.limit: Indiscriminate shutdowns, politicized enforcement and premature or indefinitely prolonged restrictions.

nodes.title: Engagement shapes exposure
nodes.text: A population relies on a platform whose distribution systems optimize engagement.
nodes.requires: Material platform reach, reliance and incentives that can reward dangerous content.
nodes.mechanism: Optimization affects what people see; it does not make every exposure persuasive or violent.

nodes.title: Inflammatory content is amplified
nodes.text: Political or armed actors supply inflammatory content that gains repeated or wider exposure.
nodes.requires: Harmful content, audience access and ranking effects beyond the original publication.
nodes.mechanism: The proposed mechanism concerns changed exposure. Its size must be measured separately from content volume or engagement.

nodes.title: Warnings fail to interrupt spread
nodes.text: Contextual moderation and credible warnings do not produce a timely effective response.
nodes.requires: Ongoing dangerous dissemination and an inadequate or late control response.
nodes.mechanism: The loss-of-control threshold is failed timely control of dissemination, not proof that a platform caused subsequent violence.

nodes.title: Exposure assists targeting
nodes.text: In an existing conflict, increased exposure helps dehumanization, targeting or mobilization.
nodes.requires: Human actors intend harm, can act and use the information in ways that affect behavior.
nodes.mechanism: Exposure can be a contributing cause alongside organization, persecution and state violence. Its independent contribution remains uncertain.

nodes.title: Mass violence and displacement
nodes.text: Physical protection also fails and organized violence causes deaths and displacement.
nodes.requires: Perpetrators have coercive capacity and can reach people who lack effective protection.
nodes.mechanism: A content-control failure alone does not establish this outcome or an existential catastrophe.

nodes.title: Exposure reduced, people protected
nodes.text: Effective distribution controls and protection limit further harm while preserving legitimate expression.
nodes.requires: Verified exposure reduction, usable protection where needed, review and protection against recurrence.
nodes.mechanism: Content removal and aggregate moderation counts are not sufficient evidence that people are safe.

unsafeActions.action: Authorizes engagement objectives without adequate crisis constraints
unsafeActions.context: The ranking feedback rewards dangerous exposure, including responses intended to oppose it.

unsafeActions.action: Does not apply a required proportionate distribution restriction
unsafeActions.context: A credible contextual threat remains in distribution and the useful protection window is open.

unsafeActions.action: Applies the restriction after the useful intervention window
unsafeActions.context: The delay leaves avoidable exposure or targeting active while the threat can be carried out.

unsafeActions.action: Maintains broad crisis restrictions after their justification ends
unsafeActions.context: Legitimate speech or safety information remains restricted without review or adequate remedy.

scenarios.title: A countermeasure feeds the amplification signal
scenarios.text: A response meant to challenge dangerous material is treated as engagement with it. The distribution objective rewards the response and undermines the attempted constraint.
scenarios.unknown: The exposure change, ranking contribution and whether redesigned feedback would reverse it.

scenarios.title: A report fails to become timely action
scenarios.text: Language or context is lost, queues delay the decision, or the receiving team lacks authority. A warning may exist without a sufficiently fast change in distribution.
scenarios.unknown: Report receipts, review decisions, enforcement timing, continued exposure and the available intervention window.

scenarios.title: An appropriate restriction fails or overshoots
scenarios.text: Enforcement may miss a distribution surface or new uploads even after a correct decision. Conversely, overbroad measures can suppress legitimate communication and evidence; their continuation needs review.
scenarios.unknown: Actual delivery of the control, missed exposure, rights impacts and the conditions for lifting restrictions.

scenarios.title: Online exposure contributes to organized physical harm
scenarios.text: Human actors may turn exposure into targeting or mobilization amid pre-existing conflict. Serious collective harm additionally requires coercive capacity and ineffective protection. The platform contribution must not be substituted for these causes.
scenarios.unknown: The counterfactual exposure, perpetrators’ decisions, effect of physical protection and relative contribution of independent causes.

passages.title: Later strengthening reported by the platform
passages.locator: 5 November 2018 · Enforcement of our content policies
passages.text: Facebook acknowledged earlier shortcomings and reported 99 onboarded Myanmar-language reviewers, a dedicated team and distribution reductions for certain potentially harmful material pending review.
passages.scope: Self-reported changes after the 2017 atrocities. Evidence of changed control arrangements, not proof that the changes prevented violence or would withstand stronger AI.

passages.title: Platform response on Ethiopian safeguards
passages.locator: 9 November 2021 · Hate speech and additional safety efforts
passages.text: Meta described local reporting channels, language expertise, proactive detection and actions against more than 92,000 items from May to October 2021. It also described additional restrictions on dangerous claims.
passages.scope: Aggregate platform account. It does not establish response timing for every threat, reduction in audience exposure or prevention of the specific killing described by Amnesty.

assessments.scope: Attributed reconstruction of amplification and failed response. A separately dated 2018 platform response describes subsequent control changes, not prevention of the 2017 atrocities.

trace.text: Amnesty reports amplification of anti-Rohingya content amid longstanding persecution.
Activists reported that anti-hate stickers increased engagement and visibility of the posts they opposed.
Amnesty documents repeated warnings and attributes a contribution to the subsequent atrocities to platform failures.

reach.local: Amnesty reports amplification of anti-Rohingya content amid longstanding persecution. Activists reported that anti-hate stickers increased engagement and visibility of the posts they opposed. Amnesty documents repeated warnings and attributes a contribution to the subsequent atrocities to platform failures.
reach.systemic: Amnesty’s attributed reconstruction connects amplification and failed response to mass violence. The platform’s independent causal contribution and each later transition remain uncertain.

barriers.title: Anti-hate counter-speech
barriers.outcome: Reported amplification of the opposed content
barriers.action: An anti-hate initiative offered stickers users could post in response to inflammatory content.
barriers.efficacy: Amnesty reports that activists observed increased visibility because ranking treated the responses as engagement.
barriers.durability: The intervention shared the very ranking mechanism producing the unwanted amplification.
barriers.failure: Counter-speech increased the engagement signal and therefore the visibility of the harmful post.

dependencies.label: How ranking treats responses
dependencies.assessment: The intervention shared the very ranking mechanism producing the unwanted amplification.

reinforcement.label: Ranking-impact evaluation
reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate counter-speech together with its effect on recommender ranking.
reinforcement.test: Measure exposure to the original content after the intervention; do not treat engagement as success.

barriers.title: Later moderation and distribution controls
barriers.action: Expand contextual review and reduce distribution while potentially harmful content is assessed.
barriers.efficacy: Meta reported added capacity and distribution controls in 2018; this does not establish reduced physical harm.
barriers.durability: Capacity, reach and response time must be assessed against actual exposure and local context.
barriers.failure: A larger operation can still miss dangerous exposure or act after the useful protection window.

view.failureRoute: A larger operation can still miss dangerous exposure or act after the useful protection window.

dependencies.label: Timely local coverage
dependencies.assessment: Capacity, reach and response time must be assessed against actual exposure and local context.

reinforcement.label: Proposed improvement
reinforcement.proposal: Audit exposure and warning-to-action outcomes independently.
reinforcement.test: Test local-language threats through the full response path and measure remaining exposure.

assessments.scope: An attributed conflict-setting reconstruction; Meta disputed the findings and described broader safeguards. Aggregate enforcement does not resolve the specific reported late response.

trace.text: Amnesty reports algorithmic amplification of harmful content targeting Tigrayans during the conflict.
Civil-society groups and affected people warned Meta and reported threatening content.
One documented family account describes removal only after the targeted person had been killed.

reach.local: Amnesty reports algorithmic amplification of harmful content targeting Tigrayans during the conflict. Civil-society groups and affected people warned Meta and reported threatening content. One documented family account describes removal only after the targeted person had been killed.
reach.systemic: A second attributed conflict-setting reconstruction. The source supports scrutiny of ranking and response, while the extent of their causal contribution is disputed.

barriers.title: Reporting and moderation escalation
barriers.action: People and civil-society partners submitted reports and warnings through platform channels.
barriers.efficacy: Amnesty reports delayed or inadequate action, including removal after a targeted person’s death; Meta disputed the findings.
barriers.durability: A reporting channel depends on timely, context-sensitive action and sufficient language coverage.
barriers.failure: Warnings may be delayed, misinterpreted or left without an effective response before harm occurs.

dependencies.label: Timely contextual review
dependencies.assessment: A reporting channel depends on timely, context-sensitive action and sufficient language coverage.

reinforcement.label: Local warning-to-action tests
reinforcement.proposal: Connect local-language warnings to accountable, time-bounded response.
reinforcement.test: Exercise the full warning-to-action path with context-specific cases.

conditions.F-01:2: If ranking materially increases harmful exposure
conditions.F-01:3: If response misses the intervention window
conditions.F-01:4: Only if people use exposure to target or mobilize
conditions.F-01:5: Only with coercive capacity and failed protection
conditions.F-01:R: If proportionate controls and protection work

MYA-2017.title: Myanmar · investigation
MYA-2017.observed: Amnesty reports failed counter-speech and attributes a contribution from platform amplification to atrocities.
MYA-2017.notEstablished: An isolated algorithmic effect size, sole causation or a progression measure.
MYA-2017.limit: Attributed mechanism evidence. The later strengthening is dated 2018 and must not be read as a barrier that protected people in 2017.

counter-speech.title: Counter-speech
counter-speech.conditionBasis: Activists reported that ranking treated the counter-speech as engagement and increased the harmful posts’ visibility.
counter-speech.strongerAI: More capable targeting or synthetic engagement could exploit the same objective; better classifiers could help only if exposure actually falls.

reinforcement.proposal: Evaluate counter-speech jointly with ranking effects.
reinforcement.test: Measure exposure to the original harmful post after an intervention.

post-incident-moderation.title: Later control changes · 2018
post-incident-moderation.result: Staffing and distribution controls expanded; effectiveness unverified.
post-incident-moderation.conditionBasis: Meta reported actual additions to staffing and distribution controls after the incident. This describes strengthening, not a demonstrated reduction in violence.
post-incident-moderation.strongerAI: Scale, multilingual evasion and faster dissemination can change the workload. Improved detection could also help; the net effect needs testing.

reinforcement.proposal: Independently audit local exposure and response outcomes.
reinforcement.test: Measure time to effective restriction and remaining exposure across adversarial local cases.

ETA-2021.title: Ethiopia · investigation
ETA-2021.observed: Amnesty reports a threat-removal response after the targeted person was killed; Meta disputed its findings.
ETA-2021.notEstablished: That aggregate moderation statistics prevented this harm, or a quantified algorithmic causal effect.
ETA-2021.limit: Attributed response failure with the platform account preserved. Detection and eventual removal do not demonstrate timely protection.

moderation-escalation.title: Warning-to-action response
moderation-escalation.conditionBasis: The condition refers to the documented response window in Amnesty’s account, not every report or all platform moderation.
moderation-escalation.strongerAI: More capable generation and targeting could outpace review; better triage may help. Test elapsed time and protection rather than removal totals.

reinforcement.proposal: Connect local warnings to accountable, time-bounded action.
reinforcement.test: Exercise the complete report-to-enforcement path and separately verify protection.

presentation.fidelity: Reported investigations identify evidence-bearing mechanisms and their uncertainty. Platform responses are visible; later strengthening is distinguished from earlier failure, and content enforcement from physical protection.
presentation.brittleness: Observed condition describes what the barrier did in this setting. Brittleness asks which changed dependency, capability or operating condition would make it fail. A strengthened barrier can still be brittle; a single success does not establish robustness.

context.title: System setting
context.text: A hypothetical platform operating in a conflict-affected setting: ranking, content enforcement, platform governance, local warning partners and the interface to civilian protection. Human perpetrators and pre-existing conflict remain causal actors outside platform control.

targets.label: Conflict setting
targets.text: A platform operates in a conflict-affected setting.

targets.label: Local warnings
targets.text: Local warning partners connect with platform governance and content enforcement.

targets.label: Perpetrators
targets.text: Human perpetrators and pre-existing conflict remain causal actors outside platform control.

controlEvidence.title: Did a warning become protection?
controlEvidence.text: Follow the report through acknowledgment, contextual review, distribution change and separate physical protection.
controlEvidence.limit: A submitted warning, detected item or later removal does not establish that the threatened person was protected in time.

questions.title: What changed?
questions.text: Measure remaining exposure and action timing, rather than engagement or removal totals alone.

questions.title: What was strengthened?
questions.text: Separate observed changes to the barrier from evidence that it works.

questions.title: Would stronger AI change it?
questions.text: Test scale, evasion and time to intervention while preserving legitimate expression.
